title: The White Hurricane of 1913 and the Michigan City pier

sources.what: Storm Nov. 7-10, 1913; peak Nov. 9; a dozen ships sunk; roughly 250 sailors lost, most on Lake Huron; only one vessel lost on Lake Michigan, the barge Plymouth near Green Bay
sources.who: NWS Detroit; NWS Great Lakes retrospective; Lake Carriers' Association 1913 report

sources.what: Chicago: Lincoln Park breakwater swept away; waterfront damage
sources.who: Wikipedia, Great Lakes Storm of 1913; Sault Ste. Marie Evening News, Nov. 10, 1913

sources.what: Michigan City: the storm destroyed 200 feet of the elevated walk to the East Pierhead light; keepers used a breeches buoy to reach it
sources.who: Lighthousefriends; U.S. Lighthouse Society archive photos dated Nov. 18, 1913, 'Michigan City East Pierhead, Storm Damage 1913' and 'Breeches Buoy'

sources.what: Steamer Louisiana burned and sank at Washington Island, crew survived; barge Plymouth lost with all hands at the mouth of Green Bay
sources.who: Wisconsin Historical Society NRHP record; Wikipedia, Plymouth (schooner barge)

beats.text: In November 1913, the worst storm in Great Lakes history blew for four days. Here's what it did to Michigan City.
beats.label: NOVEMBER 7 TO 10, 1913
beats.credit: Sources: National Weather Service; Lake Carriers' Association

beats.text: Sailors called it the White Hurricane. Hurricane-force winds, whiteout snow, and waves taller than a house. About a dozen ships went to the bottom, and roughly 250 sailors died, most of them on Lake Huron.
beats.label: THE WHITE HURRICANE

card.label: NOVEMBER 9, 1913
card.note: SAILORS LOST, A DOZEN SHIPS SUNK

beats.credit: Sources: NWS Great Lakes retrospective; Lake Carriers' Association, 1913

beats.text: At the south end of Lake Michigan, Chicago's brand-new Lincoln Park breakwater was wrecked.
beats.label: CHICAGO'S LAKEFRONT
beats.credit: Sources: Wikipedia; Sault Ste. Marie Evening News, Nov. 10, 1913

beats.text: And in Michigan City, the waves tore away about 200 feet of the elevated catwalk out to the East Pierhead lighthouse.
beats.label: MICHIGAN CITY'S EAST PIER

card.label: MICHIGAN CITY
card.note: OF THE PIER CATWALK, TORN AWAY

beats.credit: Source: Lighthousefriends; U.S. Lighthouse Society photos, Nov. 18, 1913

beats.text: To reach the light, the keepers rode a breeches buoy: a canvas seat on a rope, slung over the gap, above the surf.
beats.label: THE KEEPERS' COMMUTE

typed.text: A SEAT ON A ROPE, OVER THE WAVES.

beats.credit: Source: U.S. Lighthouse Society archive, 'Breeches Buoy,' 1913

beats.text: No ship was lost anywhere near Michigan City. The only one lost with her crew on Lake Michigan went down at the mouth of Green Bay. But the lighthouse that guided boats home that week is still standing on the pier today.
beats.credit: All pictures drawn. Sources: NWS; Lake Carriers' Association; Lighthousefriends
